keyframes.prompt: Vertical 2:3 nature photo of a shallow seasonal floodplain pond in Africa in the rainy season, shown as a cut-away side view. The lower 45 percent of the frame is a side cross-section of soft wet dark grey-brown mud, with fine texture, a few tiny air holes and thin pale roots; the mud surface is a flat line at 45 percent of the frame height. From 45 to 80 percent of the frame height is a clear side view through still tea-brown water with fine floating particles; the water surface is a flat line at 80 percent of the frame height. The top 20 percent of the frame shows a soft blurred green African savanna with a few acacia trees under a pale blue sky. Two thin green reed stems rise from the mud near the left side, up through the water and above the surface. Soft natural daylight from the upper left, sharp focus on the mud and the water. In the mud cross-section, at the horizontal center of the frame, there is a U-shaped nest burrow filled with tea-brown water: both openings are on the mud surface, about one quarter of the frame width apart, the tube is about one twelfth of the frame width wide, and the bottom of the U reaches down to 15 percent of the frame height. At the bottom of the U lies a small cluster of about twenty round pale yellow eggs, each about one sixtieth of the frame width. A large adult male West African lungfish rests on the mud surface directly above the burrow, seen from the side, its body horizontal across the center of the frame and its head to the left, right above the left opening of the burrow. The lungfish has a long eel-like body, a rounded head with a blunt snout, a small eye and a wide mouth, smooth skin with scales embedded in it, an olive-brown back with large dark brown and black blotches, a pale unspotted belly, long thin thread-like pectoral and pelvic fins, and a tapered pointed tail with a low fin fringe. It is about half of the frame width long. It is not an eel and not a catfish, and it has no whiskers. Keep everything important away from the left and right edges. Only one adult fish. No text, no watermark.
